stylelint-config-standard supplies the correctness rules (unknown properties, duplicate selectors, deprecated values). The rules added below are the Phase 5 guardrail: every value that a retheme has to be able to reach must be written as a token reference, and `npm run lint:css` fails the build when one is not. That is why `defaultSeverity` is gone -- stylelint's own default is `error`, and this file no longer has debt to hold open.

Five of stylelint-config-standard's stylistic opinions are turned off or restated because this repository deliberately does not follow them. declaration-block-single-line-max-declarations and rule-empty-line-before: the stylesheets write short rules on one line and group them without blank lines on purpose. selector-class-pattern and selector-pseudo-class-no-unknown carry no CSS-module escape any more: Phase 4 left one styling lane, so every class is kebab-case or BEM with a feature prefix and `:global()`/`:local()` are no longer valid anywhere -- writing one is a mistake the lint now reports rather than a scoping tool. no-descending-specificity: a cascade built on breakpoint overrides trips it by design, and reordering the file to satisfy it would move pixels for no benefit. media-feature-range-notation: it contradicts media-feature-name-allowed-list below, which permits only max-width and max-height, so satisfying either would fail the other. color-hex-length is `long` rather than the standard's `short`: the palette writes every primitive as six digits, and `scripts/style-invariants.test.mjs` parses them that way to compare lightness, so a three-digit `#fff` would be a second spelling of a value the invariants read.

The breakpoint canon is the four max-width steps documented in docs/theming.md; min-width is allowed for one shape only -- the touch-tablet guard `(pointer: coarse) and (min-width: 761px)`, which max-width cannot express -- and is pinned to 761px, the exclusive complement of the 760px step. max-height is allowed for one shape too, the `(max-height: 650px) and (max-width: 760px)` short-viewport guard the sign-in card and the time-range popover each carry: it is a height guard rather than a width step, so it cannot fold onto the canon, and pinning its one value here keeps it from becoming a second ladder.

selector-class-pattern.message: Expected kebab-case or BEM with a feature prefix; the repository has one styling lane and no CSS modules

overrides.//: The primitive tier is the one place a value is allowed to be written down: the rules above exist to push every literal into app/styles/tokens-*.css, so firing them there asks the palette to point at itself and the token layer would carry the only violations nobody may fix. The exemption is scoped to the two token files and to the rules that name a value -- `color-no-hex`, the rgb()/hsl() disallow-list, and the font/size/radius/shadow/stacking allow-lists. Everything else still applies there, and `scripts/style-invariants.test.mjs` polices what a token file may contain far more closely than a stylesheet linter can.

The two files that may still carry `!important`, and the only two. Both fight a cascade that specificity cannot win, and each declaration is commented at its site.

app/styles/interaction.css holds the `prefers-reduced-motion` contract. It has to beat every animation and transition any rule in the application declares, including ones added later by a file it has never heard of, and `*` is the lowest specificity there is: the override exists precisely so that a stronger selector cannot opt out of it.

app/reports/reports.css holds the mobile card-mode overrides for the reports table. `.table--cards.table--cards td[data-label]:first-child` in the shared table primitive is (0,4,1) by design -- the class is doubled so card mode outranks a table's own desktop column widths -- and a report cell that needs a different padding or border below 760px would have to restate five class-level selectors to reach it. Raising the feature rule that far would make the primitive impossible to change without also changing every feature that shadows it, so the feature says `!important` once instead.
